title: Hold a spring-return safety loop while opening a bottle
instruction: Open the bottle and keep it upright on the table.
context: The safety loop springs back to the locking position when released. Opening requires maintaining its release while operating the separate rocker, rather than completing the releases sequentially. This tests simultaneous contact constraints during everyday assistive manipulation.
setup: One empty grey steel-bodied bottle, 72 mm body diameter and approximately 282 mm closed height, in the official calibrated YAM station. Its free body is 350 g, spring-opening lid 25 g, spring-return rocker 7 g and U-shaped spring-return safety loop 6 g. Exterior geometry is unchanged; no side handle is added. Loop crown centreline diameter is 30 mm and section diameter 6 mm; rocker face diameter is 13 mm. Nominal bottle-base pose is (0.27,0,0.7480) m, upright, yaw -90 degrees, button facing -X, lid closed and safety loop raised. Gravity settles it onto the 1.10 x 1.30 x 0.06 m table, whose centre is (0.36,0,0.7175) m and top is Z=0.7475 m. The two six-axis YAM arms stand at (0,0.305,0.75) m and (0,-0.305,0.75) m, with standard parallel grippers (0-93.9 mm jaw gap). Both start at joints [0,1,1,-0.6,0,0] radians and open grippers. The official station provides room, camera stand, top and wrist cameras, lights and robot meshes; their pinned source and the procedural bottle geometry reproduce the setup. Object jitter is zero. There are no additional task objects, holding fixtures, contents or tools.
scoring: Evaluate at 20 Hz. The current score at termination counts. Each condition requires 8 consecutive control ticks (0.4 s): 1.0 if lid angle >60 degrees from closed; otherwise 0.5 if lid >15 degrees; otherwise 0.25 if safety-loop angle >=60 degrees from raised; otherwise 0. A sampled bottle-axis dot world-up <=0.90 (tilt >=25.842 degrees), bottle-base origin Z<0.7375 m (10 mm below tabletop), or geometric table support lost (the 36 mm-radius bottom disc's lowest edge must stay within 10 mm of tabletop Z=0.7475 m, with base centre X in [-0.154,0.874] m and Y in [-0.614,0.614] m), nonfinite robot/bottle state, unavailable/nonfinite wrist measurement, or wrist joint reaction force norm >100 N for 4 consecutive ticks permanently invalidates the trial and overrides credit with zero. Use the larger of the two gripper incoming-joint force norms, including gravity. Full score or invalidation ends the episode; timeout receives the current partial score. Only robot contact may manipulate the bottle; direct bottle-joint actuation, pose edits, destruction or geometry edits are outside the allowed action interface.
run_limit: 2,400 control steps (120 simulated seconds at 20 Hz); PhysX integration is 0.001 s, 50 physics substeps per control tick.
reset_notes: Load yam/task.py in the official yam_arena station with object_jitter=0 and control_hz=20. Reset root/joint states to the fixed nominal setup and YAM READY pose with open jaws; passive mechanism forces operate during 10 unscored settling ticks (0.5 s). Refresh cameras and clear time, scorer counters and invalidation history. Official CLI verification uses seed 0; no task object randomization or consumables.
fidelity: Approximate USD/PhysX four-link bottle. The loop has a passive torsion spring (0.012 N m/rad, zero-angle rest) and damping (0.002 N m s/rad); lid and rocker are spring-loaded. No detent holding torque, gravity compensation, software unlock gate or bottle pose correction. Dimensions, friction and springs are estimates. No fluids, seal deformation or breakage; wrist units inherit static-load validation, not hardware calibration.
scores: Dream-1 beta: 0.0 (2400 steps, one continuous session); scripted demo: 1.0 (309 steps, seed 0)
